1	# Pipeline state graph — audit instrument
2	
3	A derived, self-checking model of the pipeline, tied to the owner's rulings and directions, for auditing agent work
4	(mine included) before and after it is done. It is working material: **not a ruling, not registered as a check, and not
5	in a PR.** Where it says a ruling is carried or not carried by the schema, code or CI, that is a probe result you can
6	re-run; where it says a direction follows from CLAUDE.md rule 0, that is an inference an agent made. Two independent
7	adversarial passes (a Fable 5.1 agent each; the second attacked the first's findings and the repairs) have corrected
8	it; both are summarised below, and neither is proof.
9	
10	## What is here
11	
12	| file | what it is | how it is made |
13	|---|---|---|
14	| `atoms/atoms-*.jsonl` | one claim per line — the owner's rulings, ratified governance documents, process rules, CLAUDE.md — each with a **verbatim quote**, source `file:line`, modality, speaker, date, status, enforcement | extracted by reading; quotes verified mechanically; claims reviewed only on a sample |
15	| `conflicts.yaml` → `CONFLICTS.md` | the **active-conflicts register**: adjudicated disagreements between atoms, or between an atom and the mechanism, plus a table of atom statuses that lag a later ruling | hand-adjudicated; atom ids, classes and probes checked |
16	| `machines.yaml` → `STATE-GRAPH.md` §3 | state machines: who moves a row between states, under what guard | hand-authored; every guard carries a code needle re-read on each run |
17	| `STATE-GRAPH.md` §1, 2, 2a, 4–9 | stages, tables, foreign keys (including forward-pointing ones), views, writers, the UNWRITABLE set, quarantined checks, ruling-vs-mechanism probes, tree delta | **derived** from the live repo |
18	| `capabilities.yaml` → `CAPABILITIES.md` | the four-capability interrogation (mine one source across many parameters · grow the parameter base · synthesize across parameters · specify then render) | predicates evaluated against the live tree |
19	| `ATOMS.tsv`, `OPEN-QUESTIONS.tsv`, `AMBIGUITIES.tsv`, `graph.json` | flat views for grep | generated |
20	| `build_graph.py` | the generator, checker and self-test | — |
21	| `verify_atoms.py` | stand-alone quote verifier for one atoms file | — |
22	
23	`atoms-added.jsonl` (`ADD-nnn`) holds atoms added after the adversarial review; `atoms-wrk.jsonl` (`WRK-nnn`)
24	holds the 2026-08-18 owner rulings recorded in `workplan/` that the first extraction missed (many are marked PROPOSED:
25	the frame proposal is mostly the author's own text around the six rulings R1–R6).
26	
27	## Commands
28	
29	```
30	python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --check      # verify only; exit 1 on any failure
31	python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --selftest   # prove the checks can go red (mutation tests)
32	python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py              # regenerate every derived file
33	python3 workplan/pipeline-state-graph/build_graph.py --compare /path/to/other/checkout   # add a tree-vs-tree column
34	```
35	
36	Needs `pyyaml` only. Reads `data/guidebook.db` read-only. Every figure in the generated files is a result; re-run
37	rather than trust one (rule 7a). `--check` prints `EXAMINED: n` for each class of subject.
38	
39	## How to use it to audit yourself
40	
41	1. **Before acting**, name the object (table, verb, check, document). Find its stage and writers in `STATE-GRAPH.md` §4
42	   and, if it holds a status, its machine in §3. A transition the machine does not list, or lists as having no writer,
43	   is a finding, not a licence.
44	2. **Find the rulings that bind it:** `grep -i '<term>' workplan/pipeline-state-graph/ATOMS.tsv`. Prefer `OWNER_QUOTED`
45	   over `OWNER_RELAYED` over `RATIFIED_DOC`; an `AGENT_PROPOSAL` is not a ruling even where later text relies on it.
46	   `SUPERSEDED` is history (`status_evidence` and `superseded_by` say why). **`AMENDED` is not history:** the quote is
47	   either the amended, live form or the pre-amendment form that a later ruling changed in part — read
48	   `status_evidence`/`ambiguity` to see which. `.ignore` hides `sessions/` from the Grep tool; this table does not.
49	3. **Check the register:** if the atoms you rely on appear in a `CONFLICTS.md` entry whose direction is `UNSETTLED`,
50	   do not pick a side — put it to the owner. If the direction is stated, it is an inference from rule 0, not a ruling;
51	   say so when you act on it.
52	4. **Check the mechanism, not the prose.** A `FAIL` or `NOT-BUILT` probe means the ruling is not carried by the schema,
53	   code or CI, so compliance is yours (the rule 5 / rule 7 "you are the gate" case). A `PASS` means the probe could see
54	   the thing and found it; it does not mean the ruling is fully carried. Several probes are lexical (P-H, P-O,
55	   P-STATUS-WRITERS) and the register says so.
56	5. **After acting**, run `--check`. If you changed a guard, a vocabulary or a ruling-bearing file, regenerate and read
57	   the diff of `CONFLICTS.md` and the probe table.
58	
59	## What the checks prove, and what they do not
60	
61	- **Proved mechanically:** each atom's quote occurs verbatim in its source, within three lines of the cited line; each conflict cites atoms that exist and
62	  probes that exist; each machine's state set (or `vocabs:` entry) equals the column's own CHECK, and the count of
63	  abstract machines with no single column is printed; each transition's guard still appears in the cited function (or,
64	  for `absent: true`, still does not); every stage assignment is complete and agrees with the contract; every probe ran
65	  and its source contains a literal path that can return PASS (or INFO) -- a reachability lint, **not** evidence that the
66	  probe tests the right thing: P-R passed that lint while testing the wrong function and reporting a built feature as
67	  not built; each status correction's `current` status is re-read and each deciding atom must exist, be dated no
68	  earlier than the atom it corrects, and not itself be superseded -- nothing checks that it says what `why` claims. `--selftest` shows these checks fail when what they guard is broken,
69	  including a mutation of probe reachability, of a capability verdict and of the stage map.
70	- **Not proved:** that an atom's `claim` is a fair reading of its quote (an adversarial pass drew 40 atoms at random
71	  and found 2 unfair, which were repaired; the remaining atoms are unaudited beyond that sample); that a conflict's
72	  direction is right (the same pass found several direction and speaker errors in the S1 entries, which were repaired
73	  and re-checked against the sources); that the transition guards are all the guards; that a lexical probe has no
74	  false negative. These are judgments, and each conflict records its confidence.
75	- **The adversarial passes** are reviews by other agents, not proofs. Pass 1 found direction, speaker and probe errors
76	  in the severity-1 entries; pass 2 found one false probe verdict (P-R), a settlement resting on an unsourced relay
77	  (C-027), mis-tagged speakers and statuses (CLM-*, EVI-059/060, WRK-199/200/201/204/222), and a machine edge that
78	  contradicted its own guard (M08), and sampled 30 of the workplan atoms (3 failures). The repairs were applied, the
79	  remaining workplan atoms were **not** re-audited beyond that sample, and C-029, C-032, C-034 and C-039 were not
80	  re-read by pass 2 beyond their atom lists.
81	
82	## Known gaps in coverage
83	
84	- `references/project-standards.md` lines 300–512 were read through an agent, not first-hand.
85	- Domain-content rules (door widths, thermal ranges and the like in `references/`) are **out of scope**: the graph models
86	  the pipeline, not the guidebook's design content.
87	- `workplan/`: the three ruling-bearing files named in the operative instrument's supersession table
88	  (`2026-08-18-research-frame-proposal.md`, `2026-08-18-handoff-next-session.md`,
89	  `2026-08-20-adversarial-adjudication-a18-aut.md`) are atomised (`WRK-`). The two documents it labels OPERATIVE
90	  execution plans (`2026-08-22-master-execution-plan.md`, `2026-08-22-agonist-antagonist-execution-plan.md`) and the
91	  rest of `workplan/` are **not** atomised.
92	- Atoms record what a document says. A later ruling that supersedes a document without marking it is carried in
93	  `ambiguity` and in `conflicts.yaml`, not in `status`. About thirty quotes appear in more than one atom (a ledger entry
94	  restating a DR); `--check` prints the distinct-quote count.
95	- The generator describes the checkout it is run in. The unreleased tooling branch is a column via `--compare`.
96	
97	## Process note
98	
99	Run the generator from the repository root. Calling it (or any other command) with the working directory inside this
100	folder made the transcript-preservation hook write a copy of the transcripts under it, and a `git add` of the folder
101	committed that copy; it was removed in a later commit, but the blobs remain in the branch's history.
102	
103	## Status
104	
105	Committed to the working branch; not registered in `governance/check-registry.yaml`. PR #171 (batch-24 research) was merged
106	on 2026-10-10, so the instrument and the workplan are the only unmerged content; they contain no research rows and ship as
107	their own tooling-and-documents PR (CLAUDE.md rule 10). If kept, `--check` is the candidate registry entry (it prints `EXAMINED:`, reads the repo only, and has a
108	self-test). The owner decides whether to keep it.
109

1	# Capability interrogation
2	
3	_Rendered from `capabilities.yaml` by `build_graph.py`. Each predicate is evaluated against the live tree (a probe, a verb, a needle in code, a column's CHECK, a row count) or marked HAND-ASSESSED. `CAN` = every predicate passes; `BLOCKED` = at least one fails or its construct does not exist; `UNKNOWN` = no failure but a predicate could not be decided._
4	
5	The four capabilities are stated by the owner as what the pipeline must be able to do, not as a checklist of verbs.
6	A capability is judged here as CAN only if every predicate holds on the tree being examined; a single FAIL or a
7	construct that does not exist makes it BLOCKED, and the blocking predicates are named. The verdicts describe the
8	checkout the generator was run in; `--compare` adds a second tree (the unreleased tooling branch) as a column.
9	Predicates answer "can the machinery do this at all", not "has it been done": the live row counts are in
10	STATE-GRAPH.md. A predicate that tests a ruling the mechanism does not carry fails even where a workaround exists
11	(a hand-written migration is not the pipeline).
12	
13	## Summary
14	
15	| capability | this tree |
16	|---|---|
17	| C1 Mine one source across many parameters | **BLOCKED** |
18	| C2 Grow its own parameter base | **BLOCKED** |
19	| C3 Synthesize across parameters | **BLOCKED** |
20	| C4 Specify, then render | **BLOCKED** |
21	
22	## C1 Mine one source across many parameters
23	
24	Can a single admitted source be read once and yield values for several parameters, in every lens, with a
25	record of what was and was not looked for -- without the slug it happened to be filed under limiting what
26	is taken from it (owner, 2026-10-09: "every admitted source is scanned for any and all applicable parameters,
27	whatever slug it was filed under")?
28	
29	| pred | says | verdict | why | atoms |
30	|---|---|---|---|---|
31	| C1.1 | no UNIQUE(ref_id) on the capture table: one source may yield many rows | **PASS** | P-D = PASS | LED-100, LED-101 |
32	| C1.2 | a phrase can be harvested from a source without presupposing a category | **PASS** | matched | LED-115, CLM-040 |
33	| C1.3 | one source can be harvested for more than one sense of the same phrase | **FAIL** | P-W = FAIL | LED-197 |
34	| C1.4 | an extraction can be filed under a slug other than the one the source was admitted to | **FAIL** | P-V2 = FAIL | LED-196, LED-201 |
35	| C1.5 | a record exists of which parameters a source has been read for | **NOT-BUILT** | P-V = NOT-BUILT | LED-195, LED-199 |
36	| C1.6 | a value can be stated in every lens, including the medical lens | **FAIL** | P-MEDICAL = FAIL | LED-110, LED-154 |
37	| C1.7 | arguments and qualitative findings can be captured as well as numbers | **PASS** | source_value_extractions.claim_type admits qualitative | SES-022, SES-023 |
38	| C1.8 | a search records which slug x lens cells it covered | **FAIL** | P-M = FAIL | LED-084, RES-04 |
39	
40	## C2 Grow its own parameter base
41	
42	Can a concept met in a source become a parameter, and can the parameter list be extended, corrected, retired
43	and merged, through sanctioned writers and with the warrant recorded -- without a container that states its own
44	answer and without hand SQL?
45	
46	| pred | says | verdict | why | atoms |
47	|---|---|---|---|---|
48	| C2.1 | a new concept enters only as a term minted from an observation | **PASS** | verb add-term declared on this tree | LED-150, LED-203 |
49	| C2.2 | a name may not state its own answer | **PASS** | matched | LED-148, PIP-16 |
50	| C2.3 | an adjudicated term can be promoted to a parameter | **PASS** | verb add-parameter declared on this tree | LED-092 |
51	| C2.4 | a term can be judged not-a-parameter, with the reason on record | **PASS** | verb decline-parameter declared on this tree | RES-16 |
52	| C2.5 | a parameter can be retired or merged on record (retire in place) | **FAIL** | P-PARAM-LIFECYCLE = FAIL | LED-169, LED-170 |
53	| C2.6 | the list can be prepopulated from earlier catalogues under screening and owner approval | **NOT-BUILT** | verb mint-term-from-catalogue absent on this tree | LED-204, LED-205 |
54	| C2.7 | which direction is better for a disabled person can be recorded per parameter | **PASS** | verb set-parameter-direction declared on this tree | LED-091 |
55	| C2.8 | the base vocabularies a parameter and a lens point into have a sanctioned writer | **FAIL** | P-O = FAIL | LED-182, CLM-031 |
56	
57	## C3 Synthesize across parameters
58	
59	Can the machinery combine what independent sources say about one parameter into a determination, show where
60	they diverge, and relate more than one parameter to another (interaction, compounding, conflict) -- so that a
61	finding that depends on two parameters has a place to be recorded and a source to be traced to?
62	
63	| pred | says | verdict | why | atoms |
64	|---|---|---|---|---|
65	| C3.1 | independent sources for one (parameter x lens) cell are combined into one state | **PASS** | matched | LED-151, PIP-08 |
66	| C3.2 | divergence between sources is a recorded state | **PASS** | convergence_assessment.status admits divergent | MIS-06 |
67	| C3.3 | a spread across lenses is carried with each lens's direction | **PASS** | matched | LED-176 |
68	| C3.4 | findings plus a threshold can reach a determination | **PASS** | P-R = PASS | LED-174, LED-172 |
69	| C3.5 | a synthesis-stage structure can relate two or more parameters | **FAIL** | P-X = FAIL | LED-097, LED-098 |
70	
71	## C4 Specify, then render
72	
73	Can a determination be computed from the evidence, keyed on parameter x lens, written through a migration,
74	retired and redetermined; and can what is written be rendered to a reader at its stated strength, from the
75	database, with the rendering gated?
76	
77	| pred | says | verdict | why | atoms |
78	|---|---|---|---|---|
79	| C4.1 | a determination is keyed on parameter_id x at least one lens | **PASS** | P-Y = PASS | LED-091, LED-130 |
80	| C4.2 | the state is computed by the engine from tier arithmetic | **PASS** | P-ENG-T3 = PASS | LED-151, LED-152, LED-010 |
81	| C4.3 | a determination can be written today: no NOT NULL foreign key of specifications points into an emptied table | **PASS** | specifications has no NOT NULL FK into an emptied table | CLM-034 |
82	| C4.4 | the engine can assign every value of the state vocabulary | **FAIL** | P-ENG-STATE = FAIL | EVI-361 |
83	| C4.5 | a determination can be retired in place and redetermined | **PASS** | verb retire-specification declared on this tree | LED-169 |
84	| C4.6 | a live renderer reads parameter x lens determinations | **FAIL** | P-K = FAIL | LED-103, PIP-06 |
85	| C4.7 | the derived surfaces can be regenerated from the database | **FAIL** | P-I = FAIL | PIP-07, CLM-050 |
86	| C4.8 | the rendering invariants and tier-derivation consistency are gated | **FAIL** | P-QUARANTINE = FAIL | PIP-06, POS-03 |
87	
88	## Components against the four capabilities
89	
90	| component | stage | C1 | C2 | C3 | C4 | what it does for the capability / what stops it |
91	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
92	| Search log (log-search, search_executions) | research | PARTIAL | -- | -- | -- | logs the query and the prior; has no lens column, so R4's slug x lens coverage cannot be shown (C1.8). |
93	| Candidate staging (add-candidate, resolve-candidate) | research | -- | -- | -- | -- | holds what a search surfaced; any disposition can follow any other (M01.t3). |
94	| Source admission (add-source, supersede-source, correct-source) | evidence | PARTIAL | -- | -- | -- | admits a source to slugs; the slug link is what add-extraction later reads as its permission. |
95	| Citation mining (log-mining) | evidence | PARTIAL | -- | -- | -- | discovery of further SOURCES, not values; a separate axis from extraction (pipeline-operations section 2). |
96	| Term harvest (observe-term) | evidence | True | True | -- | -- | records any phrase a source uses, any number per source, unjudged; the entry point for new vocabulary. |
97	| Adjudication and minting (adjudicate-term, add-term) | judgment | -- | True | -- | -- | the only route from a phrase to a term; divergent judgments are allowed to stand as a contest. |
98	| Parameter registry (add-parameter, decline-parameter, set-parameter-direction) | base | -- | PARTIAL | -- | PARTIAL | creates and declines; on the main tree nothing retires or merges a parameter (C2.5). Direction is the judgment the engine cannot make. |
99	| Lens registries (populations, base_icf, access_needs, base_taxonomy_medical) | base | PARTIAL | PARTIAL | -- | PARTIAL | add-extraction refuses a lens code whose registry is empty; the medical registry is empty (C1.6) and several base tables have no verb (C2.8). |
100	| Extraction (add-extraction, derive-extraction, amend-extraction) | judgment | PARTIAL | -- | PARTIAL | True | one parameter per call; refuses a slug the source was not admitted to (C1.4); requires a lens; is what the engine gathers by parameter. |
101	| Scan ledger (source_scans, v_scan_ledger) | judgment | NO (main) / YES (unreleased branch) | -- | -- | -- | the (source x parameter) read-state record the scan contract needs; absent from the main tree (C1.5). |
102	| Determination engine (assess_cell) | specification | -- | -- | PARTIAL | True | computes state per (parameter x one lens) cell per run and emits SQL; combines sources within a cell, not across parameters (C3.5); cannot reach a determination from findings plus a threshold (C3.4). |
103	| Determination gates (raise/resolve) | specification | -- | -- | PARTIAL | PARTIAL | records that a determination disagrees with a link; carries one lens column only (P-GT). |
104	| Convergence assessment | synthesis | -- | -- | PARTIAL | -- | per-parameter convergence of independent roots; no cross-parameter form. |
105	| Connections and conflicts (add-connection, add-conflict) | synthesis | -- | -- | False | -- | free-text targets and item-layer keys; no column can name a parameter (C3.5). |
106	| Gaps (add-gap, assess_cell) | synthesis | -- | -- | PARTIAL | -- | records that a cell is pending and why; sub-vocabulary after OPEN/CLOSED is free text. |
107	| Renderers (build_site, spec_page, generate_parts, pilot_renderings, tools/*.html) | render | -- | -- | -- | False | queries that still select item-layer columns fail on the live schema (C4.6); the regenerate script reaches none of parts/ or site/ (C4.7). |
108	| Checks and gates (Layer 0) | Layer 0 | -- | -- | -- | PARTIAL | the checks that would hold rendering invariants and tier derivation are quarantined (C4.8). |

    once the data migrations up to that timestamp have replayed. That is not a
    special case bolted on for one rename — it is the real chronology, which the
    numbered/timestamped split cannot otherwise express. Several markers may be
    present; each opens another data segment.

import re, json, glob, collections
src=open('scripts/db.py').read()
verbs=sorted(set(re.findall(r'add_parser\(\s*["\']([^"\']+)["\']', src)))
logs=sorted(glob.glob('scratchpad/*/commands.jsonl'))
pat=r'python3?\s+scripts/db\.py\s+([a-z][a-z0-9-]*)'
def tally(excl):
    cnt=collections.Counter()
    for lg in logs:
        for line in open(lg, errors='replace'):
            try: d=json.loads(line)
            except: continue
            c=(d.get('command','') or '').lstrip()
            if excl=='startswith' and re.match(r'(grep|echo|cat)\b', c): continue
            if excl=='segment':
                pass
            for m in re.finditer(pat, c):
                if excl=='segment':
                    # exclude if the occurrence sits inside a segment that starts with grep/echo/cat
                    seg=c[:m.start()].split('\n')[-1]
                    seg=re.split(r'[;|&]', seg)[-1].lstrip()
                    if re.match(r'(grep|echo|cat)\b', seg): continue
                if m.group(1) in verbs: cnt[m.group(1)]+=1
    return cnt
for excl in ('none','startswith','segment'):
    c=tally(excl)
    ge10=sum(1 for v in verbs if c[v]>=10); never=[v for v in verbs if c[v]==0]
    le3=[v for v in verbs if c[v]<=3]
    print(f"excl={excl}: >=10 -> {ge10}; never -> {never}; <=3 -> {len(le3)}")
    if excl=='segment': print("  <=3:", le3); print("  synonyms", c['synonyms'], "add-medical", c['add-medical'])
PY

## Owner ruling 2026-09-16 — RETIRE IN PLACE, NEVER HARD-DELETE

> **"retire in place then"**

Given in answer to the proposal `scripts/migrations/076_never_reuse_identifiers.sql` named and
declined to smuggle in: *"The single rule that would make both unnecessary is `retire in place,
never hard-delete`, for which the mechanism is already half-built (`evidence_sources.superseded_by_ref_id`,
`base_parameters.status = 'retired'`, `source_locators.status = 'RETIRED'`) … That is a doctrine
change and an owner decision, so it is named here and not smuggled in."* It is now made. Recorded on
contact per `CLAUDE.md` rule 0; the paperwork below is what the ruling CHANGES, never an argument
against it.

**WHAT IT SUPERSEDES.** 076's framing of the two floors as permanent; any future data migration that
hard-deletes rows to retract them; and `assess_cell`'s re-determination refusal keying on NOT EXISTS,
which the same comment says "could key on NOT RETIRED" under this rule — that is now the design, not
a hypothetical.

**WHAT IT DOES NOT TOUCH, stated because the boundary is easy to over-read.** `CLAUDE.md` §8's
"Code, checks, scripts, dead tables and views: delete them" stands unchanged. This ruling governs
DATA ROWS AND IDENTIFIERS, where deleting destroys provenance the project cannot reconstruct. Git
history genuinely is the archive for code, so a deleted script loses nothing; a deleted row loses
the fact that it existed. The two are different objects and §8's removal-friendly posture on
apparatus is not weakened.

**WHY IT WAS RULED, in the owner's own framing:** *"This is a recurring provenance and data
management issue."* The floors 076 built are repairs applied after a delete has already destroyed
identity. They accumulate, and they collide: batch 08 found the thirteen RETIRED tombstones being
read as live DOI claims by BOTH `research_batch_dod.py` R9a and `db.py add-source`, so the re-run
the 2026-09-13 clearing ruling ordered could not admit a single cleared source by any route — the
only remedy either offered was to cross-file a retired identifier, which is the one thing 076 exists
to prevent. Both were fixed the same day by exempting RETIRED rows; neither fix would have been
needed had the rows never left.

**AN EXECUTION CONDITION, NOT A RE-LITIGATION.** An adversarial pass on this proposal was already in
flight when the ruling landed. Its strongest line: the views (`v_best_practice` and the rest) may not
filter on status, in which case retire-in-place would keep untrusted rows on the READING SURFACE —
which would defeat the 2026-09-13 ruling's purpose rather than serve it. That does not reopen this
ruling; it is a condition of executing it correctly. **No row is retired in place until every reader
that could surface it filters on status**, and that sweep is rule 4's ("a VIEW IS a caller") applied
to this ruling.

CONDITION: Any session about to delete a data row, retract a source, clear a corpus, or design a
supersede path; and any migration that would empty a table.
ACTION: (1) Retire in place — set the status the table already carries — never hard-delete. (2)
Before the first retirement, sweep every reader that could surface a retired row and make it filter;
a view that does not is the defect. (3) Re-key `assess_cell`'s re-determination refusal on NOT
RETIRED rather than NOT EXISTS. (4) Where a row MUST genuinely leave (owner-ordered destruction,
fabricated data), that is an exception the owner rules on case by case, and it is recorded here.
